name: Jarrod M. Hicks
intro: I study how our brains turn sounds into meaning, and I also make fun perception content.
description: Jarrod M. Hicks studies how the brain turns sound into meaning. Postdoctoral fellow at the University of Rochester.
about: I record from the human brain, measure behavior, and build computational models to understand how we make sense of sound.

Currently, I'm a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Rochester working with Sam Norman-Haignere to study the neural and computational mechanisms of invariant speech perception with support from an [NIH F32 Fellowship](https://reporter.nih.gov/search/QzmxsH50-USvNdKz_gkXcg/project-details/11459751). Before that I did my PhD at MIT with Josh McDermott, funded by an [NSF Graduate Research Fellowship](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/initiatives/grfp), studying the perception of sound textures (e.g., running water, chirping birds, wind blowing, etc.) and their role in auditory scene analysis.

Outside the lab, I enjoy teaching, outreach, and making content about perception as a [Museum of Science Digital Science Communication Fellow](https://www.mos.org/press-release/museum-science-announces-inaugural-cohort-digital-science-communication-fellows) under the name [psychophyshicks](https://youtube.com/@psychophyshicks).
